reissue.title: Reissued Bonds: Reading an Auction Result
reissue.intro: Bangladesh Bank often reissues an existing bond: it sells more of a bond it has already issued, with the same interest rate and maturity date, instead of creating a new one. That changes a few things for a buyer, so the same “5-year” label can mean very different things. Here is how to read one.

example.title: Worked Example: 5-Year Bond, 9.0% Interest
rows: Price per 100 of face value / yield
Accrued interest (23 days since last payment)
example.note: Interest is paid every six months on the original dates (9 Feb and 9 Aug) until maturity, when the principal is repaid. Bangladesh Bank deposits all of it into the client’s bank account. Amounts applied for and allotted can differ when demand is high. All figures are samples for explanation, not a real result.

points.title: Less Time Left
points.body: The bond matures on its original date, so a reissued 5-year bond may have far fewer than 5 years left.

points.title: Price Sets Your Yield
points.body: The interest rate is fixed at the original rate, but your yield also depends on the price paid (here 98.4691 per 100, giving 9.7152%).

points.title: Accrued Interest Evens Out
points.body: You pay the seller the interest earned so far, then receive the full next payment, so you are not short-changed.

points.title: Same Automatic Payments
points.body: Interest and maturity payments still go straight to your bank account with nothing for you to do.

glossary.title: New to These Terms? Quick Glossary

items.def: The return you earn by holding the bond, including the coupon payments and any difference between what you paid and what you get back.
The fixed interest rate the bond pays, every six months, until it matures.
The highest yield Bangladesh Bank accepted at an auction. Bids above it were rejected.
About how many years are left until the bond matures and you get your principal back.
When Bangladesh Bank sells more of a bond it has already issued, with the same interest rate and maturity date.
Interest the bond has earned since its last payment date. The buyer reimburses the seller at purchase and gets the full payment later.
Clean price excludes accrued interest. Dirty price includes it and is the actual cash you pay.

note.title: Good to Know
note.body: Through Midway you can apply for Treasury Bond auctions. Treasury Bills and Government Sukuk auctions are not open to brokerage clients. For now, the one Sukuk listed on the stock market can be traded through Midway. Minimum ৳1 lakh. Ask us on WhatsApp about charges.
